description_medium: The supplied account says political consultant Michael Caputo lived briefly in Kyiv in 2007 and worked on Bloc Lytvyn’s parliamentary campaign. description_long: The supplied account describes Michael Caputo as having moved from Miami Beach to Kyiv in 2007 and worked for Bloc Lytvyn in a Ukrainian parliamentary campaign. title: Unverified Draft: Alleged January 2025 Border Patrol Pardons
description_short: Internal draft: an alleged 2025 Trump pardon of Border Patrol agents convicted of migrant abuse is unverified and may duplicate another unsupported record.
description_medium: The frozen synopsis alleges Trump pardoned Border Patrol agents and other officers convicted of abusing migrants in January 2025, then claims abuse reports increased. description_long: The frozen synopsis alleges that, on or around January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump pardoned multiple Border Patrol agents and other law-enforcement officers convicted of abusing migrants. It further alleges that reports of abuse rose after the clemency and that the pardons signaled impunity. These are supplied allegations, not findings in this draft. No agents, cases, conviction dates, pardon warrants or exact clemency terms are identified. The supplied notes say the cited Associated Press page could not be accessed and that no dated dataset or organization was given for the alleged rise in reports. A separate supplied record, entry-6585, repeats the January 20 Border Patrol pardon claim; its own evidence note says the located January 20 Justice Department proclamation concerned January 6 offenses, not Border Patrol cases. That overlap does not prove either record's event, identify a survivor or justify a merger. The record therefore cannot state that the pardons happened, that abuse reports increased, or that the pardons caused an increase. It preserves the claim for internal review only; recipients, orders, complaint data and comparison period remain unresolved.

title: Unverified Draft: Alleged Trump Media Insider Selling and Retail Purchases
description_short: Internal draft: the claim that Trump Media insiders sold at a peak while retail buyers entered after the 2024 merger is unverified.
description_medium: The frozen synopsis alleges that insiders sold Trump Media shares near a peak after the March 2024 SPAC merger while retail investors bought. The packet provides no transaction records or named sellers. Its Reuters link is summarized as reporting Trump said he would not sell when his lockup expired, which does not establish what others traded.
description_long: The frozen synopsis alleges that, after Trump Media & Technology Group went public through a SPAC merger in late March 2024, insiders including Donald Trump held large share positions while retail investors bought the stock. It further claims that insiders sold near a peak after lockup restrictions expired, the price then fell, and Trump’s political profile monetized the MAGA brand at ordinary investors’ expense. These are supplied allegations, not verified findings. The packet provides no filings, seller identities, transaction dates or volumes, contemporaneous evidence of retail buying, or defined measure of the claimed price decline. Its supplied Reuters syndication reference is dated September 13, 2024, and is summarized as reporting that Trump said he did not intend to sell when his lockup expired. That source URL was not independently fetched in this run, and the supplied summary does not establish whether Trump or other insiders later sold. It cannot support a claim about other shareholders or prove investor losses or causation. The March 26 date is retained from the frozen record, not independently checked; peak timing, sales, buyers, losses and motives remain unknown.

title: Unverified Draft: Alleged April 2025 Warrantless Surveillance Order
description_short: Internal draft: the alleged April 2025 order authorizing warrantless surveillance of political opponents is unsupported by an identified order or source.
description_medium: The frozen synopsis alleges Trump signed an April 2025 executive order permitting warrantless surveillance of political opponents and says civil-liberties advocates challenged it. description_long: The frozen synopsis alleges President Donald Trump signed an executive order in April 2025 authorizing surveillance of political opponents without warrants under a broad national-security rationale. It says the measure bypassed Fourth Amendment protections and was immediately challenged by civil-liberties advocates and constitutional experts. This internal draft preserves those statements only as supplied allegations. The packet provides no order number or text, White House announcement, legal authority, implementing agency, surveillance target, named challenger or court case. It therefore does not establish that an order was signed, that surveillance occurred, or that a legal challenge followed. Related supplied records make different allegations: entry-6440 is dated March 2025 and refers to an order or internal guidance overriding FISA, while entry-6789 concerns alleged FISA Court judge changes and surveillance approvals in March. Those different dates, instruments and actions do not prove the April claim and are not substituted for it or merged with it. Until an April order is identified, neither the claimed authorization nor its legal and civil-liberties consequences can be stated as fact. April 1 remains the frozen input date, not a verified signing date.
